title: Balaam tries to profit from prophecy — Numbers 22
paragraphs: Balaam tries to profit from prophecy — Numbers 22

He opened his mouth for God…
but his heart was negotiating a price.
That is Balaam in Numbers 22.

A man who could hear from heaven, yet still lean toward the gold of Moab.
A prophet with language for God, but appetites that were not surrendered to God.
And that is what makes this story terrifying.

Because not every spiritual gift means a pure heart.
Not every anointed voice is fully yielded.
Not every man who speaks for God is free from the seduction of profit.

Balak did not come with repentance.
He came with payment.
He wanted prophecy for sale.
He wanted heaven’s words hired like a weapon.
And Balaam should have slammed the door.

But he lingered.
He entertained the offer.
He kept going back to the conversation.
That is how compromise works. It does not always begin with open rebellion. It begins with a heart that enjoys being wanted by the world.
But here’s what we miss…

God was not only confronting Balaam’s mouth.
He was exposing Balaam’s motive.
“Your way is perverse before me.” (Numbers 22:32)

That is the wound in the text.
Balaam wanted to stand near the presence of God while still flirting with the rewards of disobedience.
He wanted revelation without full surrender.
Influence without holiness.
A word from God without a crucified heart.
And some of us are closer to Balaam than we want to admit.

We will not curse Israel.
But we will still price our obedience.
We will ask what faithfulness pays.
We will measure calling by opportunity, platform, applause, and who is offering the bigger table.

But the voice of God cannot be bought.
The call of God is not for sale.
And ministry that chases reward will eventually collide with the Angel in the road.

Here is the mercy of the chapter:
God blocked Balaam before Balaam could fully destroy himself.
Even the donkey saw what the prophet refused to see.

That is grace.
Painful grace.
Embarrassing grace.
Interrupting grace.

Sometimes the mercy of God looks like a ruined deal, a closed door, a public humbling, a path you cannot force open.
Sometimes God loves you enough to stand in your way.
And that road leads us to Jesus.

Because where Balaam’s heart was divided, Christ was pure.
Where Balaam leaned toward profit, Jesus emptied Himself.
Where Balaam toyed with compromise, Jesus obeyed the Father completely.
And at the cross, Christ paid for greedy hearts, double-minded motives, and every time we tried to use holy things for selfish gain.

So repent.
Not just of wicked actions.
Repent of hidden motives.
Repent of wanting God’s name to build your own kingdom.
Repent of trying to monetize what should have been surrendered.

There is still mercy for the Balaam-hearted.
There is cleansing in the blood of Jesus.
There is restoration for the compromised.
There is a narrow road where your gift no longer leads you — Christ does.

Do not sell what was meant to be sacred.
Bow low.
Tell the truth.
Follow Jesus clean-hearted.
